   MINUTES OF JULY 18, 2022
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Vice Chair Huerta called the special meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at
6:31 P.M. on Monday, July 18, 2022, with Commissioners and staff in the Council Chamber at
City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Xie.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Cheryl Anne Cabot, Catherine Cordero, Theresa Huerta,
  and Ting Xie.
Commissioners Absent:  Bronwyn Velazquez

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Supervisor Alatorre provided information for the public on how to submit comments, and how to
request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services Commission, email all
public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT – None

3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL MINUTES

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  JULY 18, 2022
   A motion was made by Commissioner Cabot, seconded by Commissioner Xie
  to approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for
  June 6, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0-1 as follows:

  AYES:  CABOT, CORDERO, HUERTA, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  VELAZQUEZ

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. PARKS MAKE LIFE BETTER MONTH
  Supervisor Alatorre presented this item.

  Public Comment: None

  The Commission inquired about the participation for the summer activities and
  commented on the departments’ utilization of all San Gabriel parks.

  B. SMITH PARK RESOURCES DISCUSSION
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the report.

  The Commission suggested a schedule for use of the courts so that both
  pickleball and tennis players can use it. They also commented on the parking
  surrounding Smith Park and asked if an impact report would be given to
  residents. Commission questioned if the Veteran’s Memorial would mean one
  of the playgrounds would be taken out and if there is a cost analysis. They
  wondered if a band shell is needed at a small park and asked if the veterans
  would consider Vincent Lugo park. Commissioners also noted there is a
  landmark tree in the area.

  Daniel Acosta, wanted to apologize for not providing context along with the
  photos of the memorial. He thanked Manager Morales-Stevens and Director
  Perez for accurately describing their plan. He also addressed Commissioner
  Cabot and expressed his displeasure with her comments at the June
  commission meeting.

  Alfonso Contreras, stated the pickleball group is growing and therefore need
  more space to play.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  JULY 18, 2022
   Larry Wang, requested more space to play pickleball in order to teach
  beginners.

  Sonia Lyn, expressed the pickleball group wholeheartedly support staff’s
  proposal for a third court.

  Commissioner Cabot thanked the pickleball players for being respectful during
  their comments. In regards to the veterans’ memorial, she does not agree with
  removing a playground for a bandshell. She does not believe the park needs
  one since the city uses temporary stages for events.

  Vice Chair Huerta likes the idea of a memorial and appreciates their endearment
  to Smith Park. She supports an area but not a bandshell that would take a large
  portion of the park. She acknowledged she did not consider that an area of the
  park is dedicated to the Tongva Gabrieleño and is concerned with the pickelball
  courts affecting that space.

  The Commission also discussed the court striping and asked if it would be
  difficult for tennis players to play with the dual striping.

  A motion was made by Vice-Chair Huerta, seconded by Commissioner Cordero to
  approve staff’s recommendation to build additional permanent pickleball court,
  including community outreach for striping and requests that the coalition consider a
  smaller, more passive project without a bandshell or move the memorial to another
  park if they want to keep the bandshell.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0-1 as follows:

  AYES:  CABOT, CORDERO, HUERTA, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  VELAZQUEZ

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  August 1, 2022

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Public Works Department Staff

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  WATER USAGE IN CITY PARKS

In an effort to reduce water use at San Gabriel’s parks, the Public Works Parks Division is
currently following all local water guidelines and requirements at Marshall, Smith and
Vincent Lugo Parks. Park lawns, planters, medians and parkways have minimized water
usage.

Park lawns are watered twice per week. Planters that do not contain draught tolerant
plants are watered once per week. Drought tolerant plants are watered once per month.
All City medians that consist of drought tolerant or low water use plantings are watered
by drip irrigation once a week, as well as trees that are on bubbler systems. The Parks
Division has begun to eliminate turf watering in some of the parkways, such as Lugo Park
adjacent to Wells Street, with the intention of planting drought tolerant shrubs in the
future.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  August 1, 2022

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Community Services Department Staff

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Monthly Department Report

Youth Programs
Summer Parks with a Mission – The Summer Parks with a Mission program at McKinley
and Roosevelt Schools concluded in July. This program served 102 youth participants.
Staff did an excellent job planning and implementing activities, and engaging participants
at the various school sites.

After School Program – Registration for the After School Program at Coolidge, McKinley,
Roosevelt, Washington and Wilson Elementary Schools began August 1. The program
begins on the first day of school, August 17. This program is available for youth in grades
1-5. The program will be newly offered at Roosevelt Elementary School for youth in grades
K-5. This program offers homework help, arts and crafts, games and recreational activities.
